$comment: Contract for data/tables/physical_relations.csv. Checked by build/src/schema.js.
title: Physical relations
description: One row per ordering that physics fixes between two properties: the lower one cannot exceed the higher one when both are measured in the same test. The rows are the one list the data lint (MEAS-PHYSICS-ORDER, MEAS-PHYSICS-HDT-LOADS) reads for published measurements, and the headline definitions' lower bounds (headline_definitions.csv) are their projection onto a material's headline: the build refuses a headline bound that no relation with Scope headline or both covers (RELATIONS-HEADLINE-DRIFT). A relation judges the values a sheet prints for one product; the estimate model's bounds are separate and looser.

fields.name: Lower property
fields.description: The property that cannot exceed the higher one (beyond the margin).

fields.name: Higher property
fields.description: The property that is at least the lower one. It may be the same property as the lower one where a test load orders the two results (HDT at 1.8 MPa and at 0.45 MPa).

fields.name: Lower load MPa
fields.description: Test load the lower value must state, within 5 %. Not applicable: any load, or a property with none.

fields.name: Higher load MPa
fields.description: Test load the higher value must state, within 5 %. Not applicable: any load, or a property with none.

fields.name: Same test
fields.description: What the two values must share for the pair to apply. A source prints a dry and a conditioned table, an XY and a Z column, a bar and a film: values across such a divide are two claims about two things, not one of them on the wrong line.

fields.name: Relative margin
fields.description: The lower value may exceed the higher one by this fraction of the higher one before the pair is a finding: lower > higher x (1 + relative margin) + absolute margin. Two different tests cross by a little where the polymer puts them close, and which comes first is scatter.

fields.name: Absolute margin
fields.description: The lower value may exceed the higher one by this much, in the normalized unit, before the pair is a finding: the rounding of a printed value, or the scatter of a transition measured twice.

fields.name: Applies to
fields.description: Which materials the relation holds for, in the syntax of properties.csv: 'Morphology: semicrystalline' (a melting point means something only there) or 'Morphology: amorphous | semicrystalline | not modelled' (every morphology but elastomer), the morphology being that of the polymer the material's Estimate identity names (polymers.csv). Blank: all materials.

fields.name: Exempt rows
fields.description: A kind of row the relation does not judge. Heavy-load Vicat: a Vicat whose own words name the heavy load (50 N, method B) as the higher value is not ordered against the glass transition, because that needle sinks into a glassy bar once it yields.

fields.name: Finding code
fields.description: The data lint code a pair that breaks the relation raises (docs/RULES.md).

fields.name: Finding on
fields.description: Which of the two measurements the finding is recorded on (and accepted against): the lower or the higher one.

fields.name: Scope
fields.description: Where the ordering is used: measurement (the lint on published values), headline (a material's headline bound, headline_definitions.csv Lower bound properties), or both.

fields.name: Basis
fields.description: One sentence of physics: why the order holds. The lint shows it after the pair, with its first letter lowered and its full stop dropped.
